node.title: Re^13: Recalcitrant placeholders
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I have asked before and the answer has always been no...

Well, you could always try providing them with this list of links...

  • [doc://perl5180delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.18] (releases 2013-2014)
  • [doc://perl5200delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.20] (releases 2014-2015)
  • [doc://perl5220delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.22] (releases 2015-2017)
  • [doc://perl5240delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.24] (releases 2016-2018)
  • [doc://perl5260delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.26] (releases 2017-2018)
  • [doc://perl5280delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.28] (releases 2018)
  • [doc://perl5320delta#Security|Security fixes in Perl 5.32] (releases 2020-2021)
With shared hosting, the inner workings of the webserver are shielded from me and I am just left to deal with my own code. With a VPS or dedicated server, much more could go wrong!

I completely understand. There are still shared webhosts out there that have better support, though - e.g. my own site and PerlMonks are both hosted by [https://www.pair.com/|Pair].
